content.text: This is a classic Benchmark path injection test case. `bar` derived from `param` flows through list operations but no sanitization, then used to build `fileName`, passed to `FileOutputStream`. This is a true positive (unsanitized path injection).

input.justification: User-controlled request parameter "BenchmarkTest01331" is stored in `param`, passed to Test.doSomething where it is placed into a list and retrieved again (no actual sanitization - just list add/remove/get operations that don't filter or validate content), returned as `bar`, then concatenated into `fileName` and used directly in `new FileOutputStream(fileName)`. There is no path validation, canonicalization check, or allow-listing performed on the tainted value before it reaches the file system sink, so an attacker can supply path traversal sequences (e.g. ../../) to write to arbitrary locations. This matches the classic OWASP Benchmark path-traversal pattern and is a genuine true positive for path injection.
